subject: Draft: consumer-friendly cross-border data handling snippet for Hosted API
messages:
From: Jessica Turner <jessica.turner@acme.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify cross-border language for Hosted API — public snippet request

Hi Tessa,

We're preparing our vendor disclosures and need a short, consumer-facing explanation of how Redwood handles cross-border data transfers for the Hosted API. Our legal team wants one paragraph we can publish in our internal procurement portal and potentially share with our privacy team. Current snippet in your DPA is quite detailed; we need a simplified version (plain language, ~2-3 sentences) that mentions subprocessors and where EU data might be routed.

Can you share something concise we can include or point me to the right public copy? Also attaching a portion of the DPA we're referencing to make the ask concrete.

Thanks,
Jessica
--
Jessica Turner
Vendor Risk Manager | Acme Corp
Attachment: requested-dpa-section.pdf (pdf)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Clarify cross-border language for Hosted API — public snippet request

Laura / Kim — forwarding Acme's request. They want a short public-facing paragraph about cross-border transfers and subprocessors for Hosted API.

Ask: 1) Can legal sign off on a 2-3 sentence consumer-friendly line that mentions: (a) data may be processed in multiple regions (including EU/US), (b) subprocessors may be used and are listed in our public subprocessor map, (c) primary controls (encryption in transit, contractual safeguards). 2) Product: can we ensure the Console privacy tooltip can accept this phrasing?

I've attached the DPA excerpt from Acme and added a quick draft in the attachment (proposed-snippet.md). If you think we should avoid the word "transfer" and use "processing locations" instead, flag it.

Thanks — can you reply with an approved snippet and any edits by EOD today so I can share with them?

— Tessa
Signature: Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Rep | Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-snippet.md (text/markdown), dpa-extracts.pdf (pdf)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify cross-border language for Hosted API — public snippet request

Tessa — thanks for the ping and draft. Quick take from product/legal perspective:

- Keep it short and concrete; avoid legalese like "data controller" unless the audience is legal.
- Prefer "processed in regions including the US and EU" over "transferred" to keep it customer-friendly.
- Must link to the public subprocessor list and the DPA for details (we can provide those links).

Proposed public snippet (2 sentences):
"Redwood may process Hosted API requests in multiple regions, including the United States and the European Union. We may engage subprocessors to help provide the service — a current list and our data protection terms (DPA) are available on our website, and all transfers are covered by contractual safeguards and encryption in transit."

Kim — any compliance red flags? If you prefer different phrasing for "subprocessors" or want to call out Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), say so.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Policy | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800

>

> - Prefer "processed in regions including the US and EU" over "transferred" to keep it customer-friendly.
> - Must link to the public subprocessor list and the DPA for details (we can provide those links).

Agree with Laura; small edits below to tighten language and make it slightly more customer-friendly. Also adding an optional one-line Console tooltip version.

Final suggested public paragraph (for website / vendor portals):
"Redwood may process Hosted API requests in multiple places, including the United States and the European Union. We sometimes use subprocessors to help run the service; the current list of subprocessors and our DPA are available online, and appropriate contractual safeguards plus encryption protect data during transfer."

Console tooltip (short):
"Requests may be processed in multiple regions; see our subprocessor list and DPA for details."

I've added both snippets to the attached proposed-snippet.md and labeled the tooltip as "console_tooltip.txt". Recommend Tessa send both to Jessica and include the links to the subprocessor page and the DPA.

— Kim
Kimberly Park
Privacy & Product Counsel | Redwood Inference
